findings.title: Two PRD claims made at the same time with different slugs get the same number
A lane can install a git hook or edit .git/info in the target and the integrity check still says unchanged
Overwriting an existing untracked file or deleting an ignored file in the target goes undetected
Taking a snapshot runs programs the repo's own git config names (fsmonitor, clean filter)
Snapshot hangs forever when a tracked file has been replaced by a FIFO
An inherited GIT_DIR makes the snapshot record another repository under the target's name
Changes inside linked worktrees and submodules of the target go unseen
A mistyped or non-repo path to the PRD allocator succeeds and builds a PRD tree in the wrong place
PRD allocation writes outside the repo through a symlinked prds directory
A slug ending in a newline is accepted and creates a file name split across two lines
A crafted before.json puts git options into the printed restore command
The restore command printed for a moved non-UTF-8 ref fails when run
Snapshot peak memory grows with the largest dirty file because it is read whole
Compare takes about 27 seconds when a lane creates 1000 refs (3 git calls per changed ref)
PRD allocator errors print a traceback and exit 1 instead of one line and exit 2
A lane's git identity is overridden by the launcher's GIT_AUTHOR_NAME, so a leaked commit does not name the lane
The README link to the agoge-gym repo is a 404
CI claims to run the same suite as release-checks but uses another Python, and release-checks hides the macOS skip
